name: reference-role-data-element-type-in-another-layer
description: A data element whose `implementation_type` names a type the model declares only in `application_types`. Since contract `8.0.0` a type field is resolved in the layer it targets alone, so a name declared in the other layer resolves to nothing there: the undeclared-type rule answers it (`interface.data-element-undeclared-type`), with the code every undeclared-target rule answers. The sibling of `reference-role-value-type-base-in-another-layer`, one role over.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model plus the application type `SyntheticTorque`. No implementation type of that name exists. The change set creates an interface whose one data element names it as an implementation type.

authorization.notes: The scope covers every create exactly, so the answer is the engine's and not the authorization boundary's.

input.intent: Carry the synthetic torque on the bus.

value.name: ISyntheticTorque
value.description: The synthetic torque on the bus

expected.notes: One address, the referrer's field, and never the target, which the layer the field targets does not declare. Either repair clears it: state the side the name is declared in (`application_type: SyntheticTorque`), or declare an implementation type of that name — which is legal since contract `8.0.0`, where it was an identity conflict before.
